question: A 2-year-old boy in a rural ICDS area is found to have Bitot's spots on examination. He has no corneal involvement. Under the National Vitamin A Supplementation Programme, which of the following correctly describes the Vitamin A prophylaxis dose schedule for a child this age?

answers.text: 1 lakh IU at 9 months, then 1 lakh IU every 6 months up to 5 years

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The 6-monthly dose from 16 months onwards is 2 lakh IU, not 1 lakh IU.

answers.text: 1 lakh IU at 9 months, then 2 lakh IU every 6 months from 16 months to 5 years

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The National Programme gives 1 lakh IU at 9 months (with measles vaccine), then 2 lakh IU every 6 months from 16 months up to 5 years of age.

answers.text: 2 lakh IU at 9 months, then 2 lakh IU every 6 months to 5 years

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The dose at 9 months is 1 lakh IU (100,000 IU), not 2 lakh IU. The higher 2-lakh IU dose begins at 16 months.

answers.text: 2 lakh IU at 9 months, then 1 lakh IU every year to 5 years

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Both the dose at 9 months and the subsequent interval are wrong. The standard schedule is 1 lakh IU at 9 months, then 2 lakh IU every 6 months.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the Vitamin A prophylaxis schedule: 1 lakh IU at 9 months (with MR/measles), then 2 lakh IU every 6 months starting at 16 months until 5 years.
Well done. The National Vitamin A Supplementation Programme gives 1 lakh IU at 9 months, then 2 lakh IU 6-monthly from 16 months to 5 years — a key examiner trap.
